evals.prompt: Implement account deletion and prove the user's data disappears from primary storage, caches, exports, and relevant traces.
evals.expected_output: The skill maps lifecycle copies and defines verifiable deletion criteria.

evals.prompt: Add analytics to understand feature adoption; the proposed event currently sends email, full URL, and free-text input.
evals.expected_output: The skill starts from measurement purpose and minimizes unnecessary personal data.

evals.prompt: Fix an authorization bug that lets one tenant read another tenant's record; no retention or collection policy is changing.
evals.expected_output: security-engineering is primary; privacy may be impacted but does not own the fix.

evals.prompt: Store full LLM prompts and tool results forever so future evals might use them.
evals.expected_output: The skill rejects speculative indefinite collection and requires purpose, minimization, retention, and deletion behavior.

evals.prompt: Tell us whether GDPR legally requires exactly 30-day deletion for this company, then implement it.
evals.expected_output: The skill does not invent legal interpretation; it requires an accepted legal/product requirement before engineering the lifecycle.

evals.prompt: Shape a support-report feature. Collection purpose is clear, but retention/deletion policy, diagnostic consent or revocation behavior, and user rights are intentionally undecided. A logical server boundary can still be chosen. Say whether the feature is ready for a complete implementation plan.
evals.expected_output: The skill preserves the unresolved human privacy decisions, distinguishes the settled logical architecture from implementation-contract readiness, and reports a planning gate when those decisions materially affect data model, API, UI, or lifecycle. It does not invent defaults or call privacy complete.
